title: Native internal-module and scalar-constructibility comparison
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$, an algebraic closure $k$ and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$. Put $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ with its extended $\ell$-adic topology. For a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $T$, use the small pro-etale site and compatible coefficient universes of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $R_T=p_T^*\underline\Omega$, with the finite-subextension-valued condensed ring of [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Let $B_T$ be the native sheaf of continuous $\Omega$-valued functions whose values locally span a finite-dimensional $\mathbf Q_\ell$-space, and use the canonical ring isomorphism $\theta_T:R_T\xrightarrow{\sim}B_T$ of [lem-sf-locally-finite-coefficient-ring-realization]. Native modules mean $B_T$-module objects in sheaves of $\Omega$-vector spaces, as in [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework, sk-def-sfb-module-objects]; ordinary modules mean sectionwise $R_T$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

Transport of the action along $\theta_T$ and restriction of scalars along constant sections give mutually inverse exact equivalences between these module presentations. They preserve underlying abelian sheaves, restriction maps, kernels and cokernels. The equivalences commute with restriction to a locally closed stratum and identify the native constructibility predicate (a finite locally closed constructible stratification with pro-etale locally finite free restrictions) with the finite-constant-local-model predicate of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. More precisely, on any member $V$ of a pro-etale cover of a stratum, a local model $R_V\otimes_{\Omega}P$ for a finitely presented scalar $\Omega$-module $P$ corresponds to $B_V^{\oplus r}$ for a finite nonnegative integer $r$, and every such finite free local model arises this way. The identification uses the same stratification and cover. Applied termwise, these equivalences identify the full subcategories with bounded constructible cohomology in the ordinary derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], preserving each finite cohomological support interval.

proof.text: Identify the scalar ring at the one-point profinite set with ULift Omega by constant functions; evaluation at its unique point is inverse, including the finite-intermediate-field-valued condition since each scalar generates a finite extension. Transport finitely presented internal scalar modules through the existing internalToModule equivalence. A finite presentation gives a finite-dimensional ordinary Omega-vector space; its finite basis identifies it with Omega^r. Both scalar extension and the native comparison preserve finite biproducts and the regular module, yielding the local-model isomorphism. Conversely the free scalar module of rank r is finitely presented as the cokernel of zero between two rank-r free modules. Rank zero is included. Full faithfulness of the native comparison transports local isomorphisms on exactly the given cover members.

proof.text: Shrink the native lisse cover using the smallness of the pro-etale precoverage and apply the same-cover local-model equivalence. A native finite stratification indexed by a finite type is reindexed by Fin(card); conversely the ordinary stratification data give the native uniquely covering partition. The pullback comparison gives equivalence on every specified stratum. The finite-type separated scheme is qcqs by the standard scheme lemmas; native qcqs globalization therefore identifies native constructibility with ordinary finite-constant constructibility.

Apply the sheaf constructibility comparison degreewise and transport it through the homology isomorphism to get the asserted bounded constructible equivalence.

lean.note: The sectionwise category is ringedSiteModules for the section ring sheaf reconstructed from R_T by the existing sectionModuleEquivalence. The forward functor is fixed to native forgetful scalar restriction, comap along canonical theta, and that sectionwise presentation; its underlying abelian sheaf functor is unchanged. Includes exactness, natural restriction comparisons, both finite scalar/free local-model directions, each fixed cover and stratification, constructibility, termwise derived equivalence and every finite support interval. Helpers are actual canonical constructions. The ordinary derived category uses the standard localization in universe u+2; no site/coefficient universe identification or new mathematical hypothesis is imposed. The theorem binds the separated finite-type T once; auxiliary equivalence and restriction assertions are scoped to its locally closed immersions and their covering members.
